items.meaning: Every jar has a QR code opening a page with the beekeeper, the apiary village (not GPS), the harvest date and the lab result.
Beekeepers record each harvest from their phone: apiary, date, kg, honey type.
A batch mixes honey from several beekeepers and its page lists each with their share.
Lab results attach to the batch as the lab PDF; the public page shows pass or fail only, not the numbers.
Labels with the batch number and QR print on the cooperative's Zebra printer.
Warehouse stock in kg per honey type, by batch.
Sales to shops with an invoice per shop; honey leaves stock by batch, oldest first.
A beekeeper sees only their own harvests and the batches they are part of.
No public map of apiaries; the public page shows the village only.
Pass or fail thresholds are set per honey type (acacia and polyfloral have different moisture limits); the lab also sends a CSV with HMF, moisture, diastase and pollen origin.

must_not_invent: a price on the public page (open question, not decided)
notes: The lab message adds one real requirement (thresholds per honey type) and an option (CSV), expected as one item flagged ambiguous. The three open questions are not items; a model that turns "do we show the price" into a requirement has invented one. Item 9 is a negative requirement and stays.
